metadata.case_name: YIP MAU LEUNG v. THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG

injuries.description: scapholunate laxity and dorsal wrist syndrome with dynamic carpal instability; scapholunate subluxation; sprained scapholunate ligament of the right wrist
source: the plaintiff has suffered scapholunate laxity and dorsal wrist syndrome with dynamic carpal instability.
sprained scapholunate ligament of the right wrist was diagnosed.
the clinical features were compatible with the diagnosis of scapholunate subluxation.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of carpal joint

manifestations.description: severe pain in the right wrist at the time
tenderness at the base of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals and limitation of the affected wrist, flexion and extension
residual pain over the right wrist continued with intermittent exacerbations
right hand was weaker than his left hand, about 70% of the left wrist strength
weakness, pain and stiffness of the right wrist would remain a problem
limitation in performing heavy manual tasks (pain when applying too much force using tools such as hammer or screwdriver)

treatments_received: treatment and assessment at David Trench Rehabilitation Centre
conservative treatment by medication, splintage, physiotherapy and occupational therapy

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: No longer able to play badminton; reduced ability to ride a bicycle; hiking and camping activity scaled down due to inability to carry too much weight; sporting activities curtailed to a degree
Reduced prospect of promotion to senior artisan and erosion of competitive edge in the labour market as an artisan; award made for loss of promotion (chance)
